items.subtopic: standard rate and digital services
items.requirement: Supplies of goods and of services to consumers in Spain are taxed at the Spanish standard VAT rate of 21%. Reduced rates of 10% and 4% exist only for specific listed supplies and do not generally cover software subscriptions, telemetry or digital services.
items.sourceTitle: Agencia Tributaria — Manual práctico IVA 2025: El tipo impositivo
items.impact: The consumer hypotheses in the product pricing model (e.g. NAV 99 EUR, HUB Pro 499 EUR) are gross figures. Treating a gross hypothesis as revenue overstates net revenue by 17.4% (1 - 1/1.21).
items.ownerAction: Apply 21% to every B2C software, telemetry and hardware line; route any proposed reduced-rate treatment to tax counsel before it enters the model.

items.subtopic: VAT-inclusive price presentation and gross-to-net conversion
items.requirement: A selling price offered to consumers is the final price including VAT and all other taxes; business invoices must state the taxable amount and the unit price exclusive of VAT. The model therefore converts a VAT-inclusive consumer hypothesis to net revenue as net = gross / 1.21.
items.sourceTitle: Directive 98/6/EC on consumer protection in the indication of the prices of products offered to consumers
items.impact: 99.00 EUR gross = 81.82 EUR net revenue + 17.18 EUR VAT. The MC-12 model must carry vatInclusive=true and the 1.21 divisor for every consumer line, otherwise contribution per SKU is overstated.
items.ownerAction: Store both gross and net in the model with the rate applied; never compare a gross consumer hypothesis with an ex-VAT supplier cost without the division.

items.subtopic: B2C place of supply and One Stop Shop (OSS)
items.requirement: For B2C supplies of digital services to consumers in other EU Member States the VAT is due in the Member State of consumption. OSS lets a trader register in one Member State and declare and pay all EU B2C supplies through a single return; OSS covers B2C operations only.
items.sourceTitle: Agencia Tributaria — Regímenes especiales de ventanilla única (OSS)
items.impact: A single 21% assumption is only valid for Spanish consumers. Cross-border EU B2C sales need the destination rate of each Member State, so average net revenue per subscription is not a Spanish-rate constant.
items.ownerAction: Register for OSS before any cross-border selling and add an unpriced OSS compliance line; keep the model segmented by destination country.

items.subtopic: B2B intra-EU reverse charge
items.requirement: Where services are supplied by a taxable person not established in the Member State of the customer, VAT is payable by the taxable customer under the reverse-charge mechanism; the supplier invoices the net amount without VAT.
items.sourceTitle: Council Directive 2006/112/EC (consolidated 14/04/2025) — place of supply of services, reverse charge
items.impact: B2B lines (distributor, yard, fleet-contract, app-store/API sales) are net-of-VAT amounts and must never be modelled as VAT-inclusive gross. Mixing B2C and B2B in one price field breaks the contribution calculation.
items.ownerAction: Separate B2C gross prices from B2B net prices in the model; validate customer VAT identifiers before invoicing.

items.subtopic: recoverable input VAT on purchases
items.requirement: VAT borne on business purchases (hosting, connectivity, licensed data, components, logistics) is deductible input VAT where the activity is taxable, under the deduction rules of Title X of the VAT Directive, subject to the Spanish prorrata rules where exempt activity exists.
items.sourceTitle: Council Directive 2006/112/EC (consolidated 14/04/2025) — Title X, deductions
items.impact: Provider tariffs quoted gross are not the P&L cost for a VAT-registered trader: the recoverable VAT is a financing/cash-flow item of up to one return period, not a permanent cost. The model must use ex-VAT cost inputs.
items.ownerAction: Normalise every supplier tariff to its ex-VAT basis and record the VAT basis of each input; add a working-capital line for VAT timing.

items.subtopic: import VAT and customs duty treatment
items.requirement: VAT on importation is chargeable when goods are imported and follows the customs-duty event; import VAT is generally recoverable by a VAT-registered importer, whereas customs duty is a cost.
items.sourceTitle: Council Directive 2006/112/EC (consolidated 14/04/2025) — Articles 70-71, chargeable event on importation
items.impact: Landed cost must split customs duty (a real cost, unknown per SKU) from import VAT (recoverable, financing only). MC-11 scenarios carry no import VAT or duty line, so landed cost is incomplete.
items.ownerAction: Model import VAT as a recoverable cash-flow item and duty as a cost once CN codes are classified; obtain a customs agent or deferment quote.

items.subtopic: customs duty rate not published per SKU
items.requirement: Customs duty is determined under the Union Customs Code by tariff classification (CN code), origin and customs value. The applicable duty rate for each MAREA hardware SKU has not been classified, so no duty rate can be stated.
items.sourceTitle: Regulation (EU) No 952/2013 — Union Customs Code
items.impact: Duty is an unpriced percentage of declared value per SKU; assuming zero duty would understate landed hardware cost. No figure is invented here: costEur stays null.
items.ownerAction: Classify each hardware SKU and its accessories, then read the duty rate in the official EU tariff tool (Access2Markets/TARIC) before any landed-cost figure is used.

items.subtopic: 3-year legal guarantee and 24-month presumption (goods)
items.requirement: Since 1 January 2022 the legal guarantee for consumer goods in Spain is 3 years; a lack of conformity appearing within 2 years of delivery is presumed to have existed at delivery. The trader is liable to repair, replace, reduce price or refund.
items.sourceTitle: Centro Europeo del Consumidor España — Garantías
items.impact: Warranty exposure runs for 36 months with a 24-month burden of proof against the seller. The MC-11 warranty allowances (1.5%/3%/6%) are labelled assumptions, not reserves derived from failure data, and must not be presented as sufficient.
items.ownerAction: Size the warranty reserve over a 36-month window and obtain bench/reliability evidence before narrowing it; show the reserve explicitly as an unknown until then.

items.subtopic: 14-day right of withdrawal in distance selling
items.requirement: In distance contracts the consumer has 14 days to withdraw without giving any reason; the trader must reimburse all payments received, including standard delivery, within 14 days of the withdrawal notice, and the consumer bears only the direct cost of returning goods unless stated otherwise.
items.sourceTitle: Directive 2011/83/EU on consumer rights — right of withdrawal and information requirements
items.impact: No-questions returns plus outbound and return shipping are a revenue and cost deduction from every online order. No observed return rate exists for MAREA, so the rate is a labelled assumption, never a measured figure.
items.ownerAction: Carry a separate returns allowance per channel and require the return-cost policy (who pays) to be decided before the model is used; mark the rate UNKNOWN.

items.subtopic: digital content withdrawal exception and refund exposure
items.requirement: The right of withdrawal can be excluded for digital content not supplied on a tangible medium only where performance began with the consumer's prior express consent and acknowledgement that the right is lost. Otherwise the 14-day refund right applies to digital purchases.
items.sourceTitle: Directive 2011/83/EU — Article 16(m), exceptions from the right of withdrawal
items.impact: Without a consent-and-acknowledgement screen at checkout, digital subscriptions carry avoidable refund exposure; with it, the exposure narrows but does not disappear for services already performed.
items.ownerAction: Specify the express-consent screen as a release requirement; until implemented, model digital refunds as open-ended.

items.subtopic: update duty and 2-year EU minimum for goods with digital elements
items.requirement: Sellers of goods with digital elements must ensure the consumer is supplied with updates, including security updates, necessary to keep the goods in conformity for the period the consumer may reasonably expect; the EU minimum seller liability is 2 years, and Spain applies the longer 3-year regime.
items.sourceTitle: Directive (EU) 2019/771 — sale of goods, conformity, updates and liability periods
items.impact: The firmware/security update duty overlaps the CRA support period and compounds the recurring engineering load. It is not a one-off certification cost.
items.ownerAction: Merge the consumer update duty and the CRA support period into one recurring firmware-maintenance cost line (quantity of releases, not price) in the MC-12 model.

items.subtopic: phased application dates and recurring support obligations
items.requirement: Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 applies from 11 December 2027, except the vulnerability and severe-incident reporting obligations which apply from 11 September 2026. Manufacturers must determine a support period of at least five years (shorter only where expected use is shorter), keep each security update available for at least 10 years or the support period, maintain a cybersecurity risk assessment and technical documentation, handle vulnerabilities and publish an SBOM-type record.
items.sourceTitle: Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 — Cyber Resilience Act
items.impact: Reporting (24-hour early warning, 72-hour notification, final report after remediation) is already live on 11 September 2026, before the main obligations. The support period and 10-year update availability make security engineering, revision control and documentation a permanent recurring cost, not a certification one-off.
items.ownerAction: Create a recurring CRA cost line for firmware/security engineering, CVD process, reporting readiness and documentation maintenance; no public price exists for these, so keep costEur null and express them in effort units.

items.subtopic: conformity assessment route and product classification
items.requirement: Products not listed as important or critical may be conformity-assessed by the manufacturer under internal control (module A) with CE marking and an EU declaration of conformity; important and critical categories require third-party assessment or certification. The CRA classification of MAREA HUB, WATCH, AIS and DISPLAY has not been established.
items.sourceTitle: Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 — conformity assessment and product categories
items.impact: If any MAREA device falls into an important class, a notified-body conformity assessment cost appears that MC-11 has never priced; if not, internal documentation and testing effort still apply. The model cannot claim either outcome today.
items.ownerAction: Obtain a written CRA classification opinion per product family before any certification budget is fixed; carry the third-party route as a downside scenario, not a cost.

items.subtopic: controller/processor roles for WATCH/FLEET telemetry
items.requirement: EMBARCARTE would be controller for account, billing, vessel and crew telemetry it determines the purposes of, and processor for data processed on a customer's instructions in FLEET tenancy. Controller-to-processor arrangements require a written Article 28 data processing agreement, including sub-processors, security measures and assistance duties.
items.sourceTitle: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 — General Data Protection Regulation
items.impact: No controller/processor decision and no DPA exists for WATCH/FLEET today. Hosting, connectivity and notification providers cannot be used lawfully in production without DPAs and a sub-processor register, so the cost is operational and recurring, not a one-off legal fee.
items.ownerAction: Decide roles per data flow, require DPAs from every processor before pilot, and add an unpriced recurring privacy-operations line (records, DPA management, subject requests).

items.subtopic: DPIA likelihood for vessel monitoring
items.requirement: A data protection impact assessment is required where processing is likely to result in a high risk, in particular for systematic monitoring, location tracking, profiling or large-scale processing of identifiable persons. Vessel tracking, crew/owner identification and behavioural analytics can meet those criteria; a DPIA must be completed before processing where it applies.
items.sourceTitle: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 — data protection impact assessment and prior consultation
items.impact: A DPIA is a gating document for FLEET/WATCH launch, not a cost line with a market price. The model must treat its absence as a launch blocker, not as zero cost.
items.ownerAction: Commission the DPIA before any telemetry pilot; if the residual risk is high, prior consultation with the AEPD is required and adds schedule, not a known cost.

items.subtopic: personal data breach notification and security incident response
items.requirement: Personal data breaches must be notified to the supervisory authority without undue delay and where feasible within 72 hours of awareness, and to affected data subjects where the risk is high; the controller must document all breaches.
items.sourceTitle: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 — notification of a personal data breach
items.impact: The 72-hour clock creates a permanent on-call, logging and forensic-readiness cost for a connected marine product; it cannot be discharged by a one-off policy document.
items.ownerAction: Add incident response, breach register and on-call rotation to the recurring operating cost list; no supplier price is public so keep the amount UNKNOWN.

items.subtopic: records, retention limits and EU data residency
items.requirement: Controllers must keep records of processing, apply storage limitation and document retention periods, and may transfer personal data outside the EEA only with an adequacy decision or appropriate safeguards. EU data residency is a design decision that supports compliance; it is not itself a GDPR requirement.
items.sourceTitle: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 — records of processing and international transfers
items.impact: Data residency, retention automation and records of processing are recurring operations costs. A supplier advertising an EU region does not by itself remove transfer or retention obligations.
items.ownerAction: Fix the retention schedule and the hosting region in the model as an operational requirement; require the provider's DPA, sub-processor list and region commitment in writing before costing hosting.

items.subtopic: consent for website storage and analytics
items.requirement: Storing or accessing information on a user's terminal equipment is allowed only with prior consent after clear information, except technical storage necessary for transmission or for a service explicitly requested; Spanish LSSI article 22.2 transposes the same consent rule for website cookies.
items.sourceTitle: Ley 34/2002 de servicios de la sociedad de la información y comercio electrónico — artículo 22.2
items.impact: Consent management affects the website's measurement and acquisition economics: analytics, retargeting and conversion measurement degrade without consent, so no conversion rate or CAC can be assumed from non-consented tracking.
items.ownerAction: Model acquisition and conversion as UNKNOWN rather than borrowing consent-inflated industry benchmarks; implement a consent banner with logged choices.

items.subtopic: PSD2 strong customer authentication and hosted/tokenised checkout
items.requirement: Strong customer authentication is required for electronic remote payment transactions, with limited risk-based exemptions; the merchant must not store card data where the payment provider hosts the checkout and returns a token. Pre-contractual consumer information must be given before the order is binding.
items.sourceTitle: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2018/389 — RTS on strong customer authentication (PSD2)
items.impact: SCA adds a redirect/authentication step that lowers completion and increases support load; hosted/tokenised checkout keeps MAREA out of card-data scope but requires the provider's schedule, which does not exist. Chargeback and refund exposure follows the refund duties in LT-009 and LT-010.
items.ownerAction: Cost the checkout from the provider's written schedule (unavailable today) and model SCA abandonment as an explicit parameter, not a constant; keep the no-card-data rule as an architecture requirement.

items.subtopic: EU Product Liability Directive 2024/2853
items.requirement: The revised Product Liability Directive (Directive (EU) 2024/2853) repeals Directive 85/374/EEC with effect from 9 December 2026, requires transposition by that date, treats software (including updates and AI systems) as a product, makes destruction or corruption of data compensable and applies a 3-year limitation period and a 10-year expiry period.
items.sourceTitle: Directive (EU) 2024/2853 on liability for defective products
items.impact: No-fault liability runs to 10 years post-placement, includes software and lost data, and cannot be capped contractually against consumers. Any risk reserve or insurance sizing is a guess until a broker quotes; no cost is invented here.
items.ownerAction: Register product liability as a standing risk with an unpriced reserve; obtain the broker's terms before the first shipped unit.

items.subtopic: product liability premium is not publicly published
items.requirement: No public tariff exists for product liability insurance covering connected marine electronics; the premium is set by underwriters from turnover, territories, certification evidence, recall exposure and claims history. The revised Product Liability Directive explicitly asks the Commission to monitor the availability of product liability insurance.
items.sourceTitle: Directive (EU) 2024/2853 — Article 20, evaluation including availability of product liability insurance
items.impact: The insurance premium is a material unknown recurring cost and must appear in the model as null/UNKNOWN, never as an assumed percentage of revenue.
items.ownerAction: Request broker indications for a marine-electronics product liability and recall cover; until a written indication exists, keep costEur null and flag the contribution margin as incomplete.

items.subtopic: AIS receive-only permitted; AIS transmission not an authorised offering
items.requirement: AIS is a regulated maritime VHF radio system (ITU-R M.1371) used within the maritime mobile service; transmitting equipment must be type-approved radio equipment with CE marking under the Radio Equipment Directive, and use of radio spectrum in Spain requires a legal title under the General Telecommunications Law (Ley 11/2022). MAREA's authorised scope is AIS reception only.
items.sourceTitle: ITU-R Recommendation M.1371-6 — technical characteristics of the VHF AIS in the maritime mobile service
items.impact: No revenue, bundle, subscription or margin may be modelled for AIS transmission, AIS transmission hardware or AIS-as-a-service. Receive-only claims must also say clearly that reception depends on other parties' transmitting equipment.
items.ownerAction: Keep AIS product copy and the model at receive-only; reject any pricing line that implies transmitting AIS. Escalate to counsel and the Spanish spectrum authority before any change.

items.subtopic: PILOT safety-critical gate is BLOCKED
items.requirement: PILOT performs safety-critical steering/control functions. Its safety gate is BLOCKED: no independent safety case, bench programme or sea-trial evidence exists, and no economic model, price, bundle or partner term may clear it. Product liability for such a product cannot be capped against consumers.
items.sourceTitle: Directive (EU) 2024/2853 — no-fault liability for defective products; internal gate: docs/marea/products/PILOT-SAFETY-CASE-OUTLINE.md
items.impact: PILOT contributes zero authorised revenue and zero modelled cost in MC-12. Any sensitivity table that includes PILOT revenue is invalid; MC-11 already carries PILOT known subtotal at 0.00.
items.ownerAction: Exclude PILOT from all pricing, bundle and contribution outputs; record the gate as BLOCKED and owner as safety engineering, not commercial.

items.subtopic: MAREA is a proposed brand; legal clearance NOT_GRANTED
items.requirement: An EU trade mark right is acquired only by registration and confers exclusive rights; use of an identical or similar sign for identical or similar goods can be prohibited. No EU or Spanish registration or clearance search has been completed for MAREA, so the brand is a proposal only.
items.sourceTitle: Regulation (EU) 2017/1001 on the European Union trade mark
items.impact: No brand-derived premium, brand-licence revenue, co-branding fee or trademark valuation may enter the model. The brand cannot be presented as registered, cleared or enforceable.
items.ownerAction: Commission an EUIPO and Spanish clearance search plus registration; keep brand value at null until a filing is granted and published.

vatRules.b2bIntraEuReverseCharge: For B2B supplies of services to a taxable customer in another EU Member State, VAT is accounted for by the customer under the reverse-charge mechanism; the supplier issues a net invoice without VAT and reports the supply as a reverse-charge intra-EU service.
vatRules.caveat: 21% is the Spanish general rate verified from Agencia Tributaria guidance; Spanish reduced rates (10% and 4%) exist only for specific listed supplies and do not generally apply to software subscriptions, telemetry or digital services. Any different rate for a specific line requires counsel confirmation before it enters the model. Cross-border B2C sales are taxed at the consumer's Member State rate, so a single 21% assumption holds only for Spanish consumers.

consumerGuarantee.economicEffect: A 36-month warranty exposure plus a 24-month presumption of non-conformity and a 14-day no-reason return right are revenue deductions on every consumer sale. The EU floor is 2 years; Spain applies the longer 3-year rule. Costs stay UNKNOWN because no failure-rate or return-rate evidence exists.

gdpr.controllerProcessor: Controller for account, billing and self-determined telemetry; processor for customer-instructed FLEET tenancy data. No controller/processor decision and no Article 28 data processing agreement exists today.

insurance.note: No quotation, broker indication or public tariff exists. The premium must not be estimated as a percentage of revenue anywhere in the model.

hardBoundaries.statement: AIS transmission is not an authorised MAREA offering.
hardBoundaries.source: ITU-R M.1371 (AIS is a regulated maritime VHF system), Directive 2014/53/EU (radio equipment approval) and Ley 11/2022 (spectrum titles); MAREA scope is receive-only and AIS transmission revenue/cost is excluded from MC-12.

hardBoundaries.statement: PILOT safety gate is BLOCKED and cannot be cleared by any economic model.
hardBoundaries.source: Internal governance: docs/marea/products/PILOT-SAFETY-CASE-OUTLINE.md and MC-11 handoff; no safety case, bench programme or sea-trial evidence exists. Directive (EU) 2024/2853 sets uncappable no-fault liability for such a product.

hardBoundaries.statement: MAREA trademark legal clearance is NOT_GRANTED.
hardBoundaries.source: No EU or Spanish registration or clearance search exists; Regulation (EU) 2017/1001 grants rights only by registration. No brand-derived pricing, licence revenue or trademark valuation is admissible.
